answer.location_description: Small 3x3 square near the top-left corner of the image, rows 1-3, columns 1-3, well away from the central blob.
answer.mechanism: Two groups of layer-1 units read the patch. Large-blob detectors (units 1, 3, 7, 8, 13, 24, 27, 28, and also 18, 20) have strong positive weights there, so a bright patch turns them on. Small-blob / background detectors (units 11, 12, 16, 17, 19, 21, 25, 26, 29, 31) have strong negative weights there, so a bright patch suppresses them. In layer 2, u1 (output weight +91) is driven by units 1, 3, 7, 24, 27 and 28 (+61 to +91) and inhibited by units 25, 16 and 12 (about -59 to -78). u9 (output weight -83) is driven by units 26, 21, 25, 16 and 19 (+71 to +99) and inhibited by unit 1 (-83). A bright patch therefore raises u1 and the other positive-output layer-2 units (u0, u8, u13), lowers u9, and pushes the logit toward 'large blob'.
answer.evidence: The 3x3 block at rows 1-3, cols 1-3 has weights of about +45 to +93 in units 1, 3, 7, 8, 13, 24, 27, 28, 18 and 20. The same block has about -44 to -99 in units 11, 12, 16, 17, 19, 21, 25, 26 and 29, and about -16 to -48 in unit 31. These magnitudes stand out sharply from the surrounding weights in the same units (mostly -40 to +40, and roughly ±30 in the noise-like units). This isolated off-centre block is far from the blob. It is the only localized structure apart from the centred ring/disc patterns. Its sign always matches the unit's role: positive in units with positive annulus (large-blob) weights, negative in units with negative annulus weights and positive background weights. Units with noise-like weights (0, 2, 4, 5, 6, 9, 10, 14, 15, 22, 23, 30) show no patch.
answer.main_feature: Blob extent: units with positive weights over an annulus of radius roughly 4-7 pixels around the centre detect large blobs. Opposing units with negative weights on that annulus and positive weights on the background respond when that ring is dark, signalling a small blob.
